cases.description: A CommonJS package reads two explicit configuration files, merges parsed strings and writes the exact application configuration through the ordinary filesystem facade.

files.main.cjs: const fs = require('node:fs'); const load = require('fixture-config'); const config = load(['.env', '.env.local']); fs.writeFileSync('config.json', JSON.stringify(config) + '\n'); console.log(config.APP, config.PORT, typeof config.PORT, config.MESSAGE.split('\n').length);
files.node_modules/fixture-config/index.cjs: const fs = require('node:fs'); const { parseEnv } = require('node:util'); module.exports = function (paths) { const merged = {}; for (const path of paths) Object.assign(merged, parseEnv(fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8'))); return merged; };
files..env:
export APP=franken
PORT=3000
MESSAGE="first\nsecond # literal"
EMPTY=
LITERAL=${HOME}

cases.description: A scoped package selects its ESM export, re-exports parseEnv through a barrel, and preserves multiline quoted data and CRLF normalization without evaluating shell-like text.

files.main.mjs: import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'; import { parseEnv, mode } from '@fixture/config'; const value = parseEnv(readFileSync('app.env', 'utf8')); writeFileSync('result.json', JSON.stringify(value) + '\n'); console.log(mode, JSON.stringify(value.MESSAGE), value.COMMAND, value.RAW);

cases.description: The same package composes parseEnv defaults with explicit parseArgs arguments, including a negative boolean, repeated values and an option terminator.

files.main.cjs: const run = require('fixture-config-cli'); const first = run(require('node:fs').readFileSync('cli.env', 'utf8'), ['--no-color', '-talpha', '-t', 'beta', '--port=9000', '--', '--literal']); console.log(JSON.stringify(first.values)); console.log(JSON.stringify(first.positionals)); console.log(first.tokens.map(token => token.index).join(',')); console.log(JSON.stringify(run('PORT=7000\nCOLOR=false', []).values));
